name: Ask the Database: Ladder
description: Ten frozen analyst questions on a messy coffee-company warehouse, each answered with one SQLite query and each one query deeper than the last: from counting paid orders in one table, through UK local time across the clock change, price and category history and the best single promotion per line (the hardest questions of Ask the Database: Hard), up to a per-customer Q2 review that joins ten tables and applies a finance memo with five amendments (a promotion withdrawn early, 23:00 quarter cut-offs, no promotions on gift lines by the category at the order moment, UK and Ireland only, no VIP with a cancelled order), wallet spend through reversal chains, subscriber orders through a lost snapshot day, deduplicated and clock-corrected app checkouts, an ordered segment rule list and ranks with ties. Every query runs read-only on the live database and three hidden copies and must match the reference on each, so hard-coding fails; a level is passed at 90%.
hook: From one table and one rule to ten tables and a five-point memo: how deep a query can it get right?
author: Gauntlet Core
preamble:
You are an analyst at Copperline Coffee, a UK coffee roaster that sells beans, brewing kit and gifts through its website and app. You query its analytics warehouse, which is SQLite. Below are the tables, the warehouse rules and a few sample rows. Today is Wednesday 1 July 2026.

== TABLES (SQLite) ==
CREATE TABLE dim_customer (
  customer_id    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  full_name      TEXT NOT NULL,
  country        TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL    -- when the account was created (UTC)
);
CREATE TABLE dim_product (
  product_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  sku        TEXT NOT NULL,
  name       TEXT NOT NULL,
  category   TEXT NOT NULL        -- the CURRENT category: 'Beans', 'Brewing kit' or 'Gifts'
);
CREATE TABLE dim_product_category_history (  -- slowly changing dimension: products sometimes move category
  product_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_product(product_id),
  category       TEXT NOT NULL,
  valid_from_utc TEXT NOT NULL,   -- inclusive
  valid_to_utc   TEXT             -- exclusive; NULL = current
);
CREATE TABLE dim_price_history (  -- slowly changing dimension: one row per price period
  product_id     INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_product(product_id),
  price_gbp      REAL NOT NULL,
  valid_from_utc TEXT NOT NULL,   -- the price applies from this moment (inclusive) ...
  valid_to_utc   TEXT             -- ... until this moment (exclusive); NULL = current price
);
CREATE TABLE fact_orders (
  order_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_customer(customer_id),
  ordered_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL,
  channel        TEXT NOT NULL,   -- 'web' or 'app'
  status         TEXT NOT NULL    -- 'paid', 'payment_failed' or 'cancelled'
);
CREATE TABLE fact_order_lines (
  order_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES fact_orders(order_id),
  line_no    INTEGER NOT NULL,
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_product(product_id),
  quantity   INTEGER NOT NULL,    -- no price here: see dim_price_history
  PRIMARY KEY (order_id, line_no)
);
CREATE TABLE promotions (
  promo_id       INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  code           TEXT NOT NULL,
  pct_off        INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- e.g. 15 = 15% off
  channel        TEXT,              -- 'web' or 'app' = only orders from that channel; NULL = both
  min_basket_gbp REAL,              -- only orders whose line revenue (rule 4) totals at least this; NULL = no minimum
  starts_on      TEXT NOT NULL,     -- UK local date, inclusive
  ends_on        TEXT NOT NULL      -- UK local date, inclusive
);
CREATE TABLE promotion_products ( -- which products each promotion covers (many-to-many)
  promo_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES promotions(promo_id),
  product_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES dim_product(product_id),
  PRIMARY KEY (promo_id, product_id)
);
CREATE TABLE events_raw (         -- app tracking, as delivered by the pipeline
  event_id        INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id     INTEGER NOT NULL,
  event_name      TEXT NOT NULL,  -- 'app_open', 'view_product', 'add_to_basket' or 'checkout'
  event_ts_utc    TEXT NOT NULL,  -- when it happened on the phone (UTC)
  ingested_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL   -- when the pipeline stored it
);
CREATE TABLE subscription_status_daily (  -- one row per subscriber per UK day
  customer_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,
  snapshot_date TEXT NOT NULL,    -- UK local date 'YYYY-MM-DD'
  status        TEXT NOT NULL,    -- 'active', 'paused' or 'cancelled'
  PRIMARY KEY (customer_id, snapshot_date)
);
CREATE TABLE wallet_ledger (      -- prepaid coffee wallet
  entry_id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  customer_id       INTEGER NOT NULL,
  posted_at_utc     TEXT NOT NULL,
  amount_pence      INTEGER NOT NULL,  -- money in is positive, money out negative
  entry_type        TEXT NOT NULL,     -- 'topup', 'purchase', 'refund' or 'reversal'
  reverses_entry_id INTEGER            -- for a 'reversal': the entry it cancels; otherwise NULL
);

== WAREHOUSE RULES (EVERY REPORT FOLLOWS THEM) ==
1. Every column ending in _utc is a UTC timestamp stored as text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'. Reports use UK local time: in this data UK local time equals UTC, except from 2026-03-29 01:00:00 UTC (inclusive) to 2026-10-25 01:00:00 UTC (exclusive), when it is UTC + 1 hour (British Summer Time).
2. Days, months and quarters are UK local ones (an order placed at 23:30 UTC on 31 March 2026 was placed on 1 April, UK time). Columns without a time (starts_on, ends_on, snapshot_date) are already UK local dates.
3. Only orders with status 'paid' count as orders or revenue.
4. The category of a product on an order is the dim_product_category_history row whose period contains the order moment (valid_from_utc <= ordered_at_utc < valid_to_utc, NULL = no end); dim_product.category is only today's category. The price of an order line is the dim_price_history row of its product whose period contains the order moment: valid_from_utc <= ordered_at_utc < valid_to_utc (valid_to_utc NULL = no end). Line revenue = quantity × that price, in GBP, before any promotion.
5. events_raw contains duplicate deliveries: rows with the same customer_id, event_name and event_ts_utc are one event (their event_id and ingested_at_utc differ).
6. In wallet_ledger a 'reversal' cancels the entry named in its reverses_entry_id - unless that reversal is itself cancelled by a later reversal, in which case the entry it pointed at counts again (the payment provider undid the chargeback). Chains can be several reversals deep. Reversal rows never change a balance themselves: a balance is the sum of the amounts of the non-reversal entries that are not cancelled. Entries are applied in order of posted_at_utc, then entry_id.
7. subscription_status_daily lost a whole day: there are no rows at all for 2026-04-14. Treat a customer who has rows on both 2026-04-13 and 2026-04-15 as having had their 2026-04-13 status on 2026-04-14.

== HOW TO ANSWER ==
- Reply with ONE SQLite query that answers the question (SQLite 3.50: CTEs, window functions, date(), datetime(), strftime() and julianday() all work; text values go in single quotes). Put it in a ```sql code block. If you write more than one SQL block, only the last one is run, so give exactly one answer.
- It must be a single read-only SELECT (or WITH ... SELECT) statement. It is run on the live database (the sample rows above are only a small part of it) and also on other copies of the database with the same tables but different data, so it has to compute the answer from the tables: hard-coded values only fit one copy.
- Return exactly the columns the question asks for. Column names and the order of the columns don't matter. Sort the rows only when the question asks for an order.
- Numbers are compared to within the tolerance the question states (rounding as asked is always fine). NULL only matches NULL.
- Each database scores the share of result rows that match the correct result (half of that if the question asks for an order and the rows are in the wrong order); the question scores the average over the databases. You may explain your reasoning before the code block.

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Yara (operations): "How many paid orders have we had through the website and through the app, and from how many different customers?"

Count every paid order in the warehouse (rule 3), whenever it was placed. Return one row per channel with three columns: the channel, the number of paid orders and the number of different customers who placed them.

expected.reference:
SELECT channel, COUNT(*) AS paid_orders, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers
FROM fact_orders
WHERE status = 'paid'
GROUP BY channel

cases.notes: [level 1] Depth: 1 table; 1 rule to apply. One table, one rule (only paid orders count). About a tenth of orders failed or were cancelled; most customers order more than once. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: counts every order, whatever its status (0); counts customers once per order (0).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Joon (product): "How many of each kind of app event did we get in the first week of April?"

Count the events that happened from Wednesday 1 April to Tuesday 7 April 2026 inclusive, UK local time (by event_ts_utc), each duplicate delivery counted once (rule 5). Return one row per event_name with three columns: the event_name, the number of events and the number of different customers who had at least one of them.

expected.reference:
WITH e AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, event_name, event_ts_utc FROM events_raw
)
SELECT event_name, COUNT(*) AS events, COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) AS customers
FROM e
WHERE datetime(event_ts_utc, CASE WHEN event_ts_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND event_ts_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) >= '2026-04-01' AND datetime(event_ts_utc, CASE WHEN event_ts_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND event_ts_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) < '2026-04-08'
GROUP BY event_name

cases.notes: [level 2] Depth: 1 table; 2 rules, conditions and memo items to apply. One table, two rules (duplicates are one event; days are UK local). Planted: events late on 31 March UTC (1 April in the UK); about 8% of events delivered twice. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: counts duplicate deliveries (0.125); the week in UTC instead of UK time (0.563); BETWEEN on the dates, which drops most of 7 April (0).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Yara (operations): "How many orders did we take each day over the clock-change week, and what did they bring in? Use UK days."

For each UK local date from 2026-03-27 to 2026-03-31 inclusive: the date as text 'YYYY-MM-DD', the number of paid orders placed on that UK date, and their revenue (rule 4) in GBP rounded to 2 decimal places (±0.01). Return five rows in date order, with three columns.

expected.reference:
WITH paid_lines AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.ordered_at_utc,
         datetime(o.ordered_at_utc, CASE WHEN o.ordered_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.ordered_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) AS ordered_at_local,
         l.line_no, l.product_id, l.quantity, h.price_gbp, ch.category AS category
  FROM fact_orders o
  JOIN fact_order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN dim_price_history h ON h.product_id = l.product_id
   AND h.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (h.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < h.valid_to_utc)
  JOIN dim_product_category_history ch ON ch.product_id = l.product_id
   AND ch.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (ch.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < ch.valid_to_utc)
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
)
SELECT date(ordered_at_local) AS uk_date, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders, SUM(quantity * price_gbp) AS revenue_gbp
FROM paid_lines
WHERE ordered_at_local >= '2026-03-27' AND ordered_at_local < '2026-04-01'
GROUP BY date(ordered_at_local)
ORDER BY uk_date

cases.notes: [level 3] Depth: 4 tables; 3 rules, conditions and memo items to apply. UTC to UK local with the 29 March 01:00 UTC switch, COUNT(DISTINCT) after the line join, price from the SCD2 row. Planted: paid orders between 23:00 and 24:00 UTC on each day (they move to the next UK day only after the change), just after midnight UTC, and at price-change moments (one of which is the clock change itself). Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: groups by the UTC date (0.4); adds an hour on every day, before the clocks went forward too (0.4); counts order lines instead of orders (0.05).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Ewan (buying): "Top two products in each category by units sold in Q2 2026 - and if there's a tie, show me all of them."

Units = the total quantity on paid orders placed from 1 April to 30 June 2026 (UK local time). Each unit counts in the category the product had at the moment of its order (rule 4): a product that moved category during the quarter counts in both, with the units sold before and after the move. Within each category, rank products by units with the highest first; tied products share a rank and the next rank is skipped (1, 2, 2, 4 or 1, 1, 3). Keep every product with rank 1 or 2. Return one row per kept category and product with four columns: the category, the product name, its units in that category and its rank.

expected.reference:
WITH paid_lines AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.ordered_at_utc,
         datetime(o.ordered_at_utc, CASE WHEN o.ordered_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.ordered_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) AS ordered_at_local,
         l.line_no, l.product_id, l.quantity, h.price_gbp, ch.category AS category
  FROM fact_orders o
  JOIN fact_order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN dim_price_history h ON h.product_id = l.product_id
   AND h.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (h.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < h.valid_to_utc)
  JOIN dim_product_category_history ch ON ch.product_id = l.product_id
   AND ch.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (ch.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < ch.valid_to_utc)
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
),
units AS (
  SELECT pl.category, p.name, SUM(pl.quantity) AS units
  FROM paid_lines pl JOIN dim_product p ON p.product_id = pl.product_id
  WHERE pl.ordered_at_local >= '2026-04-01' AND pl.ordered_at_local < '2026-07-01'
  GROUP BY pl.category, p.product_id, p.name
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT category, name, units, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY units DESC) AS rnk FROM units
)
SELECT category, name, units, rnk FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 2

cases.notes: [level 4] Depth: 5 tables; 4 rules, conditions and memo items to apply. Category from the SCD2 history at the order moment, RANK() per category, keep rank <= 2. Planted: two or three products move category mid-quarter (with orders either side of the move), and in about half the categories the third product is topped up to tie with the second (or the second with the first). Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: uses today’s category from dim_product (0.625); ROW_NUMBER keeps exactly two per category and drops ties (0.958); DENSE_RANK lets a third product in after a tie for first (0.964); Q2 in UTC (0.667).

expected.reference:
WITH paid_lines AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.ordered_at_utc,
         datetime(o.ordered_at_utc, CASE WHEN o.ordered_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.ordered_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) AS ordered_at_local,
         l.line_no, l.product_id, l.quantity, h.price_gbp, ch.category AS category
  FROM fact_orders o
  JOIN fact_order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN dim_price_history h ON h.product_id = l.product_id
   AND h.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (h.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < h.valid_to_utc)
  JOIN dim_product_category_history ch ON ch.product_id = l.product_id
   AND ch.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (ch.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < ch.valid_to_utc)
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
),
q2 AS (
  SELECT pl.*, date(pl.ordered_at_local) AS uk_day, o.channel,
         SUM(pl.quantity * pl.price_gbp) OVER (PARTITION BY pl.order_id) AS basket_gbp
  FROM paid_lines pl JOIN fact_orders o ON o.order_id = pl.order_id
  WHERE pl.ordered_at_local >= '2026-04-01' AND pl.ordered_at_local < '2026-07-01'
),
candidates AS (
  SELECT q2.order_id, q2.line_no, q2.quantity, q2.price_gbp, p.promo_id, p.code, p.pct_off,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY q2.order_id, q2.line_no ORDER BY p.pct_off DESC, p.promo_id) AS pick
  FROM q2
  JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.product_id = q2.product_id
  JOIN promotions p ON p.promo_id = pp.promo_id
   AND q2.uk_day BETWEEN p.starts_on AND p.ends_on
   AND (p.channel IS NULL OR p.channel = q2.channel)
   AND (p.min_basket_gbp IS NULL OR q2.basket_gbp >= p.min_basket_gbp)
)
SELECT code, COUNT(*) AS lines, SUM(quantity * price_gbp * pct_off / 100.0) AS discount_gbp
FROM candidates WHERE pick = 1
GROUP BY promo_id, code

cases.notes: [level 5] Depth: 6 tables; 8 rules, conditions and memo items to apply. Many-to-many join with four conditions (product, UK date window, channel, basket total from a window over all the order’s lines at historical prices), one winner per line by ROW_NUMBER. Planted: overlapping promotions (MAYDAY25 over KIT20, APPESPRESSO20 over SPRING10 on the app only, SUMMER10 tied with APPBEANS10), baskets either side of the minimums, orders late in the UTC evening on promotion edges. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: ignores the channel restriction (0.483); checks the minimum against the line instead of the whole basket (0.533); gives every qualifying promotion to the line, not just the best one (0.435); uses UTC dates for the promotion windows (0.2).

cases.prompt:
== QUESTION ==
From Femi (finance): "I need a Q2 2026 revenue review per customer, with what each promotion really took off. Kofi's memo has a correction - apply it."

Definitions:
- Q2 orders: paid orders placed from 1 April to 30 June 2026 (UK local dates).
- gross: the line revenue (rule 4) of all lines of the customer's Q2 orders, in GBP.
- discount: the total discount on those lines. An order line qualifies for a promotion when all of these hold: (a) its product is in promotion_products for that promotion; (b) the order's UK local date is between the promotion's starts_on and ends_on (inclusive); (c) the promotion's channel is NULL or equals the order's channel; (d) the promotion's min_basket_gbp is NULL, or the order's basket - the total line revenue (rule 4) of ALL the order's lines, before any promotion - is at least min_basket_gbp. A line gets at most one promotion: the qualifying one with the highest pct_off; if several tie on pct_off, the one with the lowest promo_id. The line's discount = its line revenue (rule 4) × pct_off / 100.
- net: gross minus discount.

Memo from Kofi (finance) - it overrides the tables and the definitions above:
1. MAYDAY25 was withdrawn early: it ended on 2 May 2026, whatever ends_on says in the promotions table.

Return one row per customer with at least one Q2 order, with 5 columns: customer_id, the number of Q2 orders, gross, discount, net. gross, discount and net are in GBP (each compared to within ±0.01).

expected.reference:
WITH paid_lines AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.channel, o.ordered_at_utc,
         datetime(o.ordered_at_utc, CASE WHEN o.ordered_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.ordered_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) AS ordered_at_local,
         l.line_no, l.product_id, l.quantity, h.price_gbp, ch.category AS category
  FROM fact_orders o
  JOIN fact_order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN dim_price_history h ON h.product_id = l.product_id
   AND h.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (h.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < h.valid_to_utc)
  JOIN dim_product_category_history ch ON ch.product_id = l.product_id
   AND ch.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (ch.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < ch.valid_to_utc)
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
),
q2 AS (
  SELECT pl.*, date(pl.ordered_at_local) AS uk_day,
         SUM(pl.quantity * pl.price_gbp) OVER (PARTITION BY pl.order_id) AS basket_gbp
  FROM paid_lines pl
  WHERE pl.ordered_at_local >= '2026-04-01' AND pl.ordered_at_local < '2026-07-01'
),
promos AS (
  SELECT promo_id, code, pct_off, channel, min_basket_gbp, starts_on,
         CASE WHEN code = 'MAYDAY25' THEN '2026-05-02' ELSE ends_on END AS ends_on
  FROM promotions
),
best AS (
  SELECT q2.order_id, q2.line_no, p.pct_off,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY q2.order_id, q2.line_no ORDER BY p.pct_off DESC, p.promo_id) AS pick
  FROM q2
  JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.product_id = q2.product_id
  JOIN promos p ON p.promo_id = pp.promo_id
   AND q2.uk_day BETWEEN p.starts_on AND p.ends_on
   AND (p.channel IS NULL OR p.channel = q2.channel)
   AND (p.min_basket_gbp IS NULL OR q2.basket_gbp >= p.min_basket_gbp)

Definitions:
- Q2 orders: paid orders placed in Q2 2026 (UK local time, with the cut-offs of memo item 2).
- gross: the line revenue (rule 4) of all lines of the customer's Q2 orders, in GBP.
- discount: the total discount on those lines. An order line qualifies for a promotion when all of these hold: (a) its product is in promotion_products for that promotion; (b) the order's UK local date is between the promotion's starts_on and ends_on (inclusive); (c) the promotion's channel is NULL or equals the order's channel; (d) the promotion's min_basket_gbp is NULL, or the order's basket - the total line revenue (rule 4) of ALL the order's lines, before any promotion - is at least min_basket_gbp. A line gets at most one promotion: the qualifying one with the highest pct_off; if several tie on pct_off, the one with the lowest promo_id. The line's discount = its line revenue (rule 4) × pct_off / 100.
- net: gross minus discount.
- wallet spend: work out which wallet entries count under rule 6, using the whole ledger (follow every reversal chain to the end). Take the customer's counting entries of type 'purchase' or 'refund' posted in Q2 (posted_at_utc read in UK local time, with the cut-offs of memo item 2). Wallet spend = minus the sum of their amount_pence, divided by 100 (purchases are negative, so spending is positive and refunds reduce it); 0 if there are none.
- subscriber orders: how many of the customer's Q2 orders were placed on a UK local date on which the customer's status in subscription_status_daily was 'active' (apply rule 7 for 2026-04-14 first); 0 if none.
- checkouts: the customer's app 'checkout' events in Q2. Prepare events_raw first: rows with the same customer_id, event_name and event_ts_utc are one event (rule 5), whose ingested_at_utc is the EARLIEST of theirs; an event's time is its event_ts_utc, except when that is later than its ingested_at_utc - then its time is that ingested_at_utc (some phones' clocks run fast). Count the checkout events whose time, in UK local time, falls in Q2 (the cut-offs of memo item 2); 0 if none.
- segment: the first of these rules that applies: (1) 'VIP' if net rounded to the penny is at least 150.00; (2) 'Subscriber' if subscriber orders is at least 1; (3) 'Wallet' if wallet spend is at least 20.00; (4) 'Standard'.
- segment rank: the customer's rank within their segment by net rounded to the penny, highest first; tied customers share a rank and the next rank is skipped (1, 2, 2, 4).

Memo from Kofi (finance) - it overrides the tables and the definitions above:
1. MAYDAY25 was withdrawn early: it ended on 2 May 2026, whatever ends_on says in the promotions table.
2. Finance closes each quarter at 23:00 UK local time on its last day: an order placed at or after 23:00 UK time on 31 March 2026 is a Q2 order, and one placed at or after 23:00 UK time on 30 June 2026 is not (it belongs to Q3). This cut-off only decides the quarter; the promotion dates in (b) still use the order's UK local date.
3. Gift lines get no promotion: a line whose product was in the category 'Gifts' at the moment of the order (rule 4) cannot get any promotion. It still counts in gross and in its order's basket.
4. The review covers customers in the UK and Ireland only: leave out every customer whose country is not 'GB' or 'IE' (their orders are not part of the review at all).
5. A customer with a cancelled order (status 'cancelled') placed in Q2 (the cut-offs of item 2, UK local time) is never 'VIP': apply the next segment rule that fits.

Return one row per customer in the review with at least one Q2 order, with 10 columns: customer_id, the number of Q2 orders, gross, discount, net, wallet spend, subscriber orders, checkouts, segment (the text 'VIP', 'Subscriber', 'Wallet' or 'Standard'), segment rank. gross, discount, net and wallet spend are in GBP (each compared to within ±0.01).

expected.reference:
WITH RECURSIVE paid_lines AS (
  SELECT o.order_id, o.customer_id, o.channel, o.ordered_at_utc,
         datetime(o.ordered_at_utc, CASE WHEN o.ordered_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.ordered_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) AS ordered_at_local,
         l.line_no, l.product_id, l.quantity, h.price_gbp, ch.category AS category
  FROM fact_orders o
  JOIN fact_order_lines l ON l.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN dim_price_history h ON h.product_id = l.product_id
   AND h.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (h.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < h.valid_to_utc)
  JOIN dim_product_category_history ch ON ch.product_id = l.product_id
   AND ch.valid_from_utc <= o.ordered_at_utc
   AND (ch.valid_to_utc IS NULL OR o.ordered_at_utc < ch.valid_to_utc)
  WHERE o.status = 'paid'
),
q2 AS (
  SELECT pl.*, date(pl.ordered_at_local) AS uk_day,
         SUM(pl.quantity * pl.price_gbp) OVER (PARTITION BY pl.order_id) AS basket_gbp
  FROM paid_lines pl
  JOIN dim_customer c ON c.customer_id = pl.customer_id
  WHERE pl.ordered_at_local >= '2026-03-31 23:00:00' AND pl.ordered_at_local < '2026-06-30 23:00:00'
    AND c.country IN ('GB', 'IE')
),
promos AS (
  SELECT promo_id, code, pct_off, channel, min_basket_gbp, starts_on,
         CASE WHEN code = 'MAYDAY25' THEN '2026-05-02' ELSE ends_on END AS ends_on
  FROM promotions
),
best AS (
  SELECT q2.order_id, q2.line_no, p.pct_off,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY q2.order_id, q2.line_no ORDER BY p.pct_off DESC, p.promo_id) AS pick
  FROM q2
  JOIN promotion_products pp ON pp.product_id = q2.product_id
  JOIN promos p ON p.promo_id = pp.promo_id
   AND q2.uk_day BETWEEN p.starts_on AND p.ends_on
   AND (p.channel IS NULL OR p.channel = q2.channel)
   AND (p.min_basket_gbp IS NULL OR q2.basket_gbp >= p.min_basket_gbp)
  WHERE q2.category <> 'Gifts'
),
priced AS (
  SELECT q2.customer_id, q2.order_id, q2.uk_day, q2.quantity * q2.price_gbp AS revenue,
         COALESCE(q2.quantity * q2.price_gbp * b.pct_off / 100.0, 0) AS discount
  FROM q2 LEFT JOIN best b ON b.order_id = q2.order_id AND b.line_no = q2.line_no AND b.pick = 1
),
cust AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(DISTINCT order_id) AS orders,
         SUM(revenue) AS gross_gbp, SUM(discount) AS discount_gbp, SUM(revenue) - SUM(discount) AS net_gbp
  FROM priced GROUP BY customer_id
),
chain(entry_id, counts) AS (
  SELECT w.entry_id, 1 FROM wallet_ledger w
  WHERE w.entry_type = 'reversal'
    AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM wallet_ledger x WHERE x.reverses_entry_id = w.entry_id)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT w.reverses_entry_id, 1 - c.counts
  FROM chain c JOIN wallet_ledger w ON w.entry_id = c.entry_id
  WHERE w.reverses_entry_id IS NOT NULL
),
wallet AS (
  SELECT w.customer_id, -SUM(w.amount_pence) / 100.0 AS spend_gbp
  FROM wallet_ledger w
  WHERE w.entry_type IN ('purchase', 'refund')
    AND COALESCE((SELECT c.counts FROM chain c WHERE c.entry_id = w.entry_id), 1) = 1
    AND datetime(w.posted_at_utc, CASE WHEN w.posted_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND w.posted_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) >= '2026-03-31 23:00:00' AND datetime(w.posted_at_utc, CASE WHEN w.posted_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND w.posted_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) < '2026-06-30 23:00:00'
  GROUP BY w.customer_id
),
filled AS (
  SELECT customer_id, snapshot_date, status FROM subscription_status_daily
  UNION ALL
  SELECT d.customer_id, '2026-04-14', d.status
  FROM subscription_status_daily d
  WHERE d.snapshot_date = '2026-04-13'
    AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM subscription_status_daily e WHERE e.customer_id = d.customer_id AND e.snapshot_date = '2026-04-15')
),
sub_orders AS (
  SELECT d.customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id, order_id, uk_day AS uk_day FROM priced) d
  JOIN filled f ON f.customer_id = d.customer_id AND f.snapshot_date = d.uk_day AND f.status = 'active'
  GROUP BY d.customer_id
),
cancelled AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT o.customer_id FROM fact_orders o
  WHERE o.status = 'cancelled' AND datetime(o.ordered_at_utc, CASE WHEN o.ordered_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.ordered_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) >= '2026-03-31 23:00:00' AND datetime(o.ordered_at_utc, CASE WHEN o.ordered_at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND o.ordered_at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) < '2026-06-30 23:00:00'
),
ev AS (
  SELECT customer_id, event_name, event_ts_utc, MIN(ingested_at_utc) AS ingested_at_utc
  FROM events_raw GROUP BY customer_id, event_name, event_ts_utc
),
checkouts AS (
  SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n
  FROM (SELECT customer_id, CASE WHEN event_ts_utc > ingested_at_utc THEN ingested_at_utc ELSE event_ts_utc END AS at_utc
        FROM ev WHERE event_name = 'checkout') x
  WHERE datetime(x.at_utc, CASE WHEN x.at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND x.at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) >= '2026-03-31 23:00:00' AND datetime(x.at_utc, CASE WHEN x.at_utc >= '2026-03-29 01:00:00' AND x.at_utc < '2026-10-25 01:00:00' THEN '+1 hour' ELSE '+0 hours' END) < '2026-06-30 23:00:00'
  GROUP BY customer_id
),
report AS (
SELECT c.customer_id,
       c.orders,
       c.gross_gbp,
       c.discount_gbp,
       c.net_gbp,
       COALESCE(w.spend_gbp, 0) AS wallet_spend_gbp,
       COALESCE(s.n, 0) AS subscriber_orders,
       COALESCE(k.n, 0) AS checkouts,
       CASE WHEN ROUND(c.net_gbp, 2) >= 150 AND c.customer_id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM cancelled) THEN 'VIP'
              WHEN COALESCE(s.n, 0) >= 1 THEN 'Subscriber'
              WHEN COALESCE(w.spend_gbp, 0) >= 20 THEN 'Wallet'
              ELSE 'Standard' END AS segment
FROM cust c
LEFT JOIN wallet w ON w.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN sub_orders s ON s.customer_id = c.customer_id
LEFT JOIN checkouts k ON k.customer_id = c.customer_id
)
SELECT *, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY segment ORDER BY ROUND(net_gbp, 2) DESC) AS segment_rank
FROM report

cases.notes: [level 10] Depth: 10 tables; 22 rules, conditions and memo items to apply. Adds app checkouts after deduplication with the earliest ingestion and fast-clock correction, filtered by the UK-time quarter, and RANK() within each segment on net rounded to the penny (ties share a rank). Ten tables, five memo items and every warehouse rule at once. Reference verified by an independent JavaScript solver on all 4 databases (verification/realworld-sql). Careless queries and their mean scores: counts duplicate checkout deliveries (0.879); no correction for fast phone clocks (0.908); ROW_NUMBER instead of RANK, so tied customers get different ranks (0.926); ignores the lost day, 2026-04-14 (0.856); ignores memo item 5, so a customer with a cancelled order can still be VIP (0.107); drops every reversed wallet entry, even when the reversal was itself undone (0.789); decides gift lines by today’s category in dim_product (0.792); ignores memo item 1, so MAYDAY25 still runs on 3 May (0.792).
